changelog: Cache-busting audit, prompted by a report that stale JS/CSS had already masked two fixes in this series (v3.20.5's session fix and v3.21.2's replay-speed dropdown). Traced against the actual current source rather than assumed broken: the versioned-query-string mechanism (index.php's $__assetVer, sourced from version.json's current_version, appended as ?v= to every local <script>/<link> tag) has existed since v3.20.9 and was re-verified complete -- cross-checked its module list against the real js/ directory listing (all 18 files present, none missing) and confirmed both local stylesheets (css/style.css, css/brand.css) are covered. login.php/register.php/verify.php were checked too and have no local JS/CSS references at all (self-contained pages, Google Fonts only) -- nothing to add there. updater.php has one unversioned css/style.css reference but is explicitly off-limits to edit per this project's own standing rule ('Never edit updater.php'); flagged rather than silently skipped.

The actual gap: the ?v= query string only helps if the browser re-fetches the HTML document that contains it. index.php sent no cache-control headers at all, so the page itself -- not just the assets it references -- was exactly as cacheable as any other response; a stale cached copy of index.php would keep serving old ?v=<previous-version> tags and never even request the new ones. Added Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0 and Pragma: no-cache to index.php's response, right after requireLogin(). This is the more likely explanation for a stale-asset symptom surviving the v3.20.9 fix, since that fix only ever addressed the referenced files, never the referencing page.

Net effect: the versioned-query-string mechanism was already correct and complete app-wide; this release closes the one real gap in it (the outer page being cacheable) rather than re-implementing what already existed. Updates automatically on every release with no extra step, exactly as before -- it reads current_version from version.json at request time, and this file's own current_version is what every release already bumps.
release_notes: No schema changes in this release -- nothing to migrate. Per instruction, nothing was deployed as part of this turn.
